name: Cloudflare
one_liner: Internet infrastructure platform (CDN, DNS, Workers, Zero Trust) with a very large REST API, OAuth clients and official MCP servers.
auth_notes: Scoped API tokens as Bearer; OAuth clients (auth code, PKCE) for third-party apps; legacy global API key also exists (not verified on fetched pages).
access_notes: API tokens created in dashboard on a free account; OAuth client creation needs admin-type role plus DNS verification for public clients. Client API limit 1200 req/5 min per token; some endpoints plan-gated by product.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve scoped API tokens, enormous documented REST API, documented rate limits and an official Cloudflare API MCP server. Per-product plan gating applies to some endpoints.

access.quote: Enterprise customers can also contact Cloudflare Support to raise the Client API per user, GraphQL, or API token limits to a higher value.

api_surface.quote: Client API per user/account token | 1200/5 minutes
Webhooks let you deliver Cloudflare alerts to any service that accepts HTTP callbacks.
It provides access to the entire Cloudflare API — over 2,500 endpoints across DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust

mcp.quote: The Cloudflare API MCP server ↗︎ at https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp is the only MCP server you need to work with Cloudflare.
you can find several MCP servers allowing you to connect to Cloudflare's service from an MCP client

disputes.why: Dashboard tokens on free accounts (first-pass L1 value); no gate found; Enterprise only raises limits.
Vendor docs and cloudflare GitHub org publish MCP servers, incl. API MCP at mcp.cloudflare.com.
Limits page documents 1200/5 min per token.
Notification webhooks documented (alert delivery only, not general event subscription).
Limits page lists a separate GraphQL limit.
